title: Adaptive Tuning Safeguards: Playbook for Safe Apply, Rollback, and Cost Regression Detection
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Summary: After the Optimize auto-tuner rollout on 2025-01-28 we observed a set of cost regressions and sporadic latency tail increases that were traced to an overly-aggressive batching/caching profile applied to multiple customer-facing routes. This ticket captures a prescriptive, operational playbook and a set of engineering mitigations to make future autotune changes safe-by-default and to automate reliable rollback and detection.

Goals:
- Define guardrails that prevent autosuggested tuning profiles from being applied with high blast radius.
- Implement circuit-breakers, canary strategies, and cost/regression detectors.
- Provide a documented runbook for on-call and SRE to perform quick safe-rollbacks and post-incident analysis.
- Add automated verification (dry-run + small-scale simulation) and post-apply health checks.

Scope:
- Server-side Optimize auto-tuner rules (batch size, cache TTL, KV cache bypass thresholds).
- Control-plane apply paths (safe-apply flow, approval gates).
- Observability: cost dashboards, regression alerts, SLO checks, and tracing hooks.
- Rollback automation and manual rollback steps.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting the autotune algorithms themselves (this ticket focuses on safety and ops around apply/rollback).

Proposed high-level mitigations:
1) Staged rollout with automatic roll-forward/rollback decisions: apply changes initially to a narrow canary segment (1-5% of traffic) with cost and latency SLO checks at 1m/5m/1h windows.
2) Circuit-breaker: if cost per token or p99 latency increases beyond threshold X% relative to baseline, pause auto-apply and automatically revert to last safe profile.
3) Dry-run simulator: run the proposed tuning profile on recent request traces (prefix simulation) to estimate token count, KV cache miss rate, and expected latency delta before apply.
4) Apply policy: require two approvals for >10% predicted cost savings or >5% predicted latency regression; provide an emergency bypass for on-call with audit logging.
5) Health-check suite post-apply: smoke tests, synthetic traffic, token-level cost checks, and end-to-end sample queries.
6) Alerting: immediate PagerDuty alert with prefilled incident template if regression triggers.
7) Telemetry: log applied-profile id with every request for easy attribution in downstream dashboards.

Deliverables:
- A written playbook (this ticket) with step-by-step rollback/playback instructions.
- Automation: safe-apply orchestration workflow, canary rollout planner, and automatic rollback hooks.
- Dashboard panels and query templates for cost regression and latency diagnostics.
- Unit/integration tests for dry-run simulator and safe-apply paths.

Success criteria:
- No production autotune apply can increase cost by >8% for >30m without manual approval.
- Automatic rollback completes within 2 minutes of trigger and restores baseline config for affected backend.
- Post-incident RCA and metric collection complete within 48 hours of any rollback event.

Notes on risk trade-offs:
- More conservative thresholds will slow potential savings capture; however safety-first is prioritized for customer trust.
- Dry-run simulator will not perfectly model hardware variance; it should be used as a heuristic combined with canaries.
